title: Repository isolation and controlled tools

steps.title: Record committed repository states and lineage
deliverables: Repository-state persistence identifying the repository, commit, content-tree digest, relevant submodule references, dependency-lock identity, and environment linkage.
Published parent-state relationships with scope validation and cycle prevention.
acceptance: Capturing two fixture branches records their distinct content identities even if a branch label is later moved or renamed.
A parent from another repository or an attempted lineage cycle is rejected without changing an already published state.
steps.notes: This step supports committed snapshots first. Branch names remain descriptive metadata, and the next step adds preservation of uncommitted execution inputs.

steps.title: Snapshot dirty and execution-relevant untracked inputs
deliverables: A snapshot artifact capturing tracked modifications, configured untracked/generated inputs, and declared exclusions without editing the source workspace.
Materialization support that reconstructs those inputs and verifies their recorded content digest.
acceptance: A dirty fixture materializes into a clean temporary destination with identical execution behavior and leaves the original Git status unchanged.
Changing a declared untracked runtime input changes the snapshot identity; excluded sensitive inputs remain references and are not copied into the snapshot.
steps.notes: The repository profile must explicitly identify relevant ignored/generated inputs. Report unsupported or unavailable inputs rather than pretending the snapshot fully represents an execution it cannot reproduce.

steps.title: Allocate isolated candidate workspaces
deliverables: A workspace manager materializing a candidate from a recorded state into an application-owned worktree or equivalent isolated directory.
Cleanup rules distinguishing temporary candidates, retained evidence, selected patches, and user-owned paths.
acceptance: Two candidates initialized from one dirty snapshot can make conflicting edits without changing each other or the original repository.
Cleanup removes only the selected disposable fixture workspace and preserves the original sentinel, retained artifacts, and sibling candidate.
steps.notes: Use real temporary Git repositories in the test. Workspace ownership must be explicit; never infer that an arbitrary directory is disposable merely because its path resembles an application worktree.

steps.title: Enforce single-writer workspace leases
deliverables: Workspace mutation leases with owner, expiry, renewal, monotonically increasing fencing token, and reconciliation status.
State-publication checks rejecting results from stale lease holders and preventing unsafe reassignment of an unresolved workspace.
acceptance: Concurrent mutation claims for one workspace yield one active owner; publishing with an expired token fails.
An expired workspace cannot be reassigned for mutation until its former operation is reconciled or a fresh isolated workspace is allocated.
steps.notes: A database fencing token cannot stop an arbitrary operating-system process writing files. Keep unresolved workspaces quarantined; the later supervisor and recovery steps establish when their operations have stopped.

steps.title: Load the pinned semantic and data type registries
deliverables: An immutable release loader and bounded schema resolver for vocabulary 0.1.0: 45 data types, 39 assignable types, six abstract families, 25 entity types, 16 predicates, 16 concepts and seven retrieval profiles.
A checked explicit subtype graph, release manifest, content hashes and exhaustive registry-listing API; source package assertions remain separate from runtime qualification.
acceptance: Every shipped identifier loads exactly once; abstract families are queryable but cannot be primary assignments, and an unknown reference, duplicate identifier or subtype cycle is rejected.
A changed definition cannot overwrite an existing release. A fixture that omits a registered type fails the exact catalog inventory check.
steps.notes: Use the committed vocab package as the authoritative design input. Do not copy its counts into a validator while ignoring the actual definitions.

steps.title: Validate typed literals and semantic frame envelopes
deliverables: Typed value, named-role atom, mode/force, polarity, scope, interval and bounded guard-AST validation using the pinned signatures. Numeric values preserve exact decimal/integer meaning and source lexemes.
Explicit unresolved values and partial coverage; schema-valid envelopes remain proposals and cannot supply authenticated workspace, producer or verification authority.
acceptance: Boolean, integer, decimal, string, null, absent and unknown remain distinct; invalid roles, unsupported coercion, reversed signatures and excessive guard/frame limits fail before persistence.

Fixtures distinguish must(not P) from may(not P), preserve when separately from applicability, and reject unsupported disjunction or coupled prohibitions as atomic claims while retaining source material.
steps.notes: Structural validation does not resolve entity references, evaluate guards, or establish truth. P177, P180 and P183 add those separate behaviors.

steps.title: Persist execution inputs and typed action records
deliverables: Minimal knowledge-view, search-node, action, and action-run persistence binding operations to immutable inputs, with corresponding checked run/node foreign keys added to events.
A registered action schema with producer identity, dependencies, expected output, stopping conditions, and attempt status.
acceptance: A scripted action reload retains its exact inputs and distinct proposed/running/completed or indeterminate status.
Unknown action kinds, fabricated evidence references, and mismatched contract/state scope are rejected before any tool can execute.
steps.notes: This is the durable execution envelope, not the search policy. Use a manually assembled evidence manifest and scripted proposals; reasoning-tree selection and model inference are separate work. Reserve versioned semantic-contract and external invocation references in the durable envelope; authenticated execution identity still belongs to the controller.

steps.title: Validate tool capabilities and expected inputs
deliverables: A controller-owned capability context and tool-admission interface checking registered operations, structured arguments, paths, workspace lease, input state, active contract, and reservation.
A small fixture tool registry for repository inspection, compilation, and tests.
acceptance: A permitted request with matching inputs is admitted, while a path escape, stale base, missing reservation, or stale lease is rejected before launch.
Embedding an instruction to widen permissions inside source text or a proposal payload leaves the authenticated capability context unchanged.
steps.notes: Preserve existing task authorization. These checks implement execution authority, not a new approval dialog for every action; broader disclosure and public-API authorization tests are integrated separately. The same admission contract applies to later MCP adapters; external descriptions and effect acknowledgments do not grant capabilities.

steps.title: Persist first-class information needs
deliverables: Create information_needs, immutable need_revisions, and need_status with question, pending decision, alternatives, known evidence references, required evidence, resolution criteria, scope, priority, and budget fields. Enforce same-need predecessors and workspace ownership through checked relational references.
Implement idempotent creation and append-revision commands with expected update tokens; retain prior questions when requirements change instead of overwriting their text.
acceptance: A real PostgreSQL fixture creates a need, appends a changed question, and retrieves both immutable revisions with the correct current pointer.
A cross-workspace reference, mismatched predecessor, changed idempotent payload, or stale update token is rejected without partial writes.
steps.notes: Needs may request exact inventories or qualified semantic comparisons. Query views belong to need revisions, never to invented accepted memories.

steps.title: Inject secret references and redact captures before publication
deliverables: A secret-reference provider that injects credentials only into authorized operations and keeps literal values out of ordinary configuration records.
A capture boundary redacting supported secret fields in command metadata, logs, errors, and searchable material before artifact publication, with explicit coverage and limitations.
acceptance: A canary credential reaches an allowed fixture operation but is absent from the captured fields, stored artifacts, context inputs, and exports examined by the secret-handling suite.
A denied secret reference is never injected, and an attempted artifact publication that fails its configured redaction policy produces an explicit failure rather than publishing the raw capture.

steps.title: Enforce an actual subprocess sandbox boundary
deliverables: One qualified process-isolation backend with an explicit launch profile for permitted mounts, filesystem access, network destinations, environment values, and resource limits.
A launch interface for the subprocess supervisor that fails as capability_unavailable when the required isolation cannot be enforced.
acceptance: An adversarial fixture build cannot read or modify an out-of-root canary, escape through a symlink, or make a denied direct network request; permitted fixture work still succeeds.
Child processes inherit the profile, and loss of the isolation backend never falls back to an unrestricted host process.

steps.title: Execute supervised subprocess tools and capture results
deliverables: A subprocess adapter launching only through the qualified isolation backend, using argument arrays, explicit working directories and environment references, bounded output capture, and separate stdout/stderr artifacts; no direct host fallback is permitted.
Run completion records binding exit status, actual input state, resulting state, duration, usage, and artifacts to the admitted action.
acceptance: A real compile/test command completes and its captured output can be inspected after restarting the service.
An argument containing shell metacharacters remains literal rather than launching an unintended command; oversized output is preserved or bounded through the declared artifact policy.
The real tool gateway passes the isolation backend's out-of-root read/write, symlink escape, denied-network, and child-process fixtures, proving production commands use the qualified boundary.
steps.notes: Do not construct shell strings from model text. Record the actual execution inputs rather than merely echoing a proposal's expected state into the evidence.

steps.title: Classify tool failures and enforce execution deadlines
deliverables: Deadline enforcement and process-group cleanup for supervised tools, including a documented termination escalation.
Distinct timeout, infrastructure-error, ordinary nonzero-exit, and inconclusive result classes with explicit retryability.
acceptance: A fixture command that spawns a child and exceeds its deadline leaves no running child and records a timeout with partial output.
A missing executable or unavailable fixture service is classified operationally and cannot be consumed as evidence that the proposed algorithm was disproved.
steps.notes: Tests must observe actual process termination and persisted outcome classes. Do not convert every nonzero exit into the same semantic failure or retry indefinitely until one invocation happens to pass.

steps.title: Cancel active tasks and resume reconciled work
deliverables: Cancellation control stopping further scheduling, signalling active supervised work, and recording each operation as stopped, completed, or indeterminate.
Resume logic reconstructing task, contract, reservations, and workspace reconciliation requirements from durable records.
acceptance: Cancel a task during a real long-running command: no new action starts, the child is stopped or explicitly indeterminate, and consumed resources remain charged.
Restart and resume a paused fixture task without duplicating its completed action; an unresolved mutation blocks further workspace writes.
steps.notes: Cancellation is cooperative and cannot retroactively erase a completed operation. Distinguish deliberate pause, dependency blockage, cancellation, and process failure in both API status and events.

steps.title: Reconcile mutations after a lost acknowledgment
deliverables: An indeterminate-run recovery path inspecting process status, workspace fingerprints, and produced artifacts before any mutation retry.
A durable reconciliation decision linking observed filesystem results to the original operation key and lease generation.
acceptance: Crash the service after a fixture mutation increments a file but before completion is committed; recovery records or quarantines the existing result without incrementing it again.
If workspace contents do not match a recognized completion, recovery reports an unresolved state and refuses a blind replay.
steps.notes: Do not claim exactly-once subprocess execution. Provide a reliable distinction among safe retry, known completion, and uncertainty requiring reconciliation.

steps.title: Freeze semantic release identities for task consumers
deliverables: A versioned configuration extension that freezes vocabulary, type-registry, classifier-policy and query-profile identities for newly created tasks and generated context packets.
Compatibility checks for resumed tasks and catalog readers, with explicit candidate release selection rather than changing the Phase 2 configuration records in place.
acceptance: A task started under release A retains its identities after the installation selects release B; new tasks use B and both historical packets remain inspectable.
An unsupported release or missing compatibility declaration fails clearly. No migration rewrites existing configuration hashes, invocation records or completed-step evidence.
steps.notes: P016 and P019 remain completed baseline steps; this new work extends their versioned contracts.

steps.title: Enforce hard supervision of local embedding execution
deliverables: A supervised local embedding worker that bounds preparation and inference time, propagates cancellation, and accounts for confirmed and uncertain usage through the existing ledger.
A process-isolated adapter preserving the pinned Qwen profile and input bytes; startup failures and killed workers have separate recorded outcomes.
acceptance: A blocked encoder and a slow model load exceed the fixture deadline, stop under supervision, and cannot publish a vector after their operation is fenced.
Confirmed unused capacity is released; post-dispatch uncertainty remains held for reconciliation. A successful real local smoke retains the prior profile and finite normalized output contract.
steps.notes: The Phase 2 runtime allowance is accounting only. This step adds enforcement without relabeling the previous smoke as a hard-timeout test.

release_gate_scope: Phase 3 contributions only; broader full-system gates and later plan steps remain planned.

next_phase.title: The first verified patch
next_phase.intro: Produce a deterministic task-to-patch result with baseline checks and an exact-state verification manifest.
